question: Organism that causes tuberculosis is:
explanation:
• Mycobacterium tuberculosis causes TB (acid-fast bacillus).
• Spread by airborne droplet nuclei.

question: Autoclave standard sterilization temperature and time is:
explanation:
• 121°C (15 psi) for 15-30 min is standard. 134°C for 3-4 min is flash sterilization.
• Moist heat kills spores.

question: Gram-positive bacteria appear:
explanation:
• Gram-positive retain crystal violet (purple) after Gram staining.
• Gram-negative lose it and take safranin (pink).

question: Immunity acquired after natural infection is:
explanation:
• Active natural = immunity after natural infection (e.g. chickenpox).
• Active artificial = vaccination.

question: HIV primarily affects:
explanation:
• HIV targets CD4+ T cells, leading to immunodeficiency.
• AIDS when CD4 count drops and/or opportunistic infections occur.

question: Live attenuated vaccine is:
explanation:
• BCG is live attenuated. OPV (Sabin) is live attenuated.
• Inactivated: IPV, hepatitis B, DPT components.

question: Standard precautions include:
options: B. Hand hygiene, PPE, safe injection practices, safe handling of contaminated equipment
explanation:
• Standard precautions: hand hygiene, PPE (gloves, gown, mask/eye as needed), safe injection, safe handling of linen and equipment.
• Apply to all patients.

question: Nosocomial infection means:
explanation:
• Nosocomial = hospital-acquired infection (HAI).
• Prevention: hand hygiene, asepsis, antimicrobial stewardship.

question: Culture medium used for Mycobacterium tuberculosis:
explanation:
• LJ medium is used for mycobacteria (slow growth, 4-8 weeks).
• AFB smear gives quicker result.

question: Disinfection differs from sterilization in that disinfection:
options: A. Kills all microorganisms including spores
B. Kills most pathogens but not necessarily spores
D. Is used only for instruments
explanation:
• Disinfection kills most pathogens but may not kill spores.
• Sterilization kills all forms including spores.

question: E. coli is:
explanation:
• Escherichia coli is Gram-negative bacillus. Normal gut flora; some strains pathogenic.
• UTI, diarrhea, HAI.

question: Chain of infection includes:
options: B. Infectious agent, reservoir, portal of exit, transmission, portal of entry, susceptible host
explanation:
• Break any link to prevent infection. Reservoir, exit, transmission, entry, host.
• Nursing: hand hygiene, isolation, asepsis.

question: Antibiotic that inhibits cell wall synthesis:
explanation:
• Penicillins (and cephalosporins) inhibit cell wall synthesis.
• Bactericidal against susceptible bacteria.

question: Passive immunity is obtained by:
options: B. Receiving preformed antibodies (e.g. Ig, maternal antibody)
explanation:
• Passive: preformed antibodies (IgG, Ig from mother, antitoxin). Short-lived.
• Active: infection or vaccine; long-lasting.

question: MRSA stands for:
explanation:
• MRSA: resistant to methicillin and other beta-lactams. Contact precautions.
• HAI and community-acquired.

question: Virus differs from bacteria in that virus:
options: B. Requires living host to replicate; no cell structure
C. Is always treatable with antibiotics
explanation:
• Viruses: no cell structure; need host cell to replicate. Antibiotics don't work.
• Antivirals target viral replication.

question: Hand hygiene with soap and water is preferred when:
options: B. Hands visibly soiled, after C. difficile, before eating
explanation:
• Soap and water when visibly dirty, after C. diff (spore-former), before eating.
• Alcohol rub for routine hand hygiene (when hands not soiled).

question: Hepatitis B is transmitted by:
explanation:
• HBV: blood, body fluids, sexual, perinatal. Vaccine available.
• HCV also blood-borne. HAV is fecal-oral.

question: Inactivated (killed) vaccine example:
explanation:
• Inactivated: IPV, hepatitis B, influenza (injected), DPT (toxoid/killed).
• Live: BCG, OPV, MMR, varicella.

question: Antigen-antibody reaction is basis of:
options: B. Immune recognition, vaccination, serological tests
explanation:
• Antibodies bind antigens; used in immunity, vaccines, ELISA, blood grouping.
• Specificity of immune response.

question: Spore-forming bacterium that causes hospital infection:
explanation:
• C. difficile: spore-forming; causes diarrhea; spores resist alcohol—handwash with soap.
• Contact precautions; antibiotic-associated.

question: Droplet precaution is used for:
explanation:
• Droplet: particles >5 µm; spread by cough/sneeze. Mask, private room.
• Airborne: TB, measles (smaller particles).

question: Normal flora is:
options: B. Microorganisms that normally inhabit body without causing disease
explanation:
• Normal flora: bacteria etc. that colonize body (skin, gut) and can be beneficial.
• Disruption (e.g. antibiotics) can cause infection.

question: Typhoid is caused by:
explanation:
• Salmonella typhi causes typhoid fever (fecal-oral transmission).
• Fever, abdominal pain; treat with antibiotics.

question: Cold chain is important for:
explanation:
• Cold chain: vaccines kept at recommended temp (2-8°C) from manufacture to use.
• Break in chain can reduce vaccine potency.
